root_cause.text: In `net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/verbs.c`, `rpcrdma_post_recvs()` increments `ep->re_receiving` on entry but had early-return paths that skipped the matching decrement, leaving the receive-drain refcount stuck nonzero and blocking `rpcrdma_xprt_drain()`/`rpcrdma_xprt_disconnect()` forever.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both early exits from `goto out;` to `goto out_dec;` and adds `atomic_dec_return(&ep->re_receiving)` before completion, and the CVE description explicitly says that when `rpcrdma_post_recvs()` “fails to create a work request … or otherwise exits early, we should decrement ep->re_receiving before returning” or else `re_receiving will never reach zero and the completion will never be triggered.

intent_record.how: When the receive-posting path is already active, execution now jumps to a cleanup path that presumably decrements the `re_receiving` reference/counter before exiting, rather than skipping that cleanup and returning directly.

intent_record.what: In rpcrdma_post_recvs(), the empty-work-request case changed from branching to the existing out label to branching to a different label, out_dec.
intent_record.how: When no receive work requests are available, the function now follows a different exit path, implying it will perform the additional cleanup or counter adjustment associated with out_dec instead of the simpler out path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a separate exit path to ensure `re_receiving` is decremented and completion is signaled correctly in `rpcrdma_post_recvs()`.
intent_record.what: A new label `out_dec:` was inserted just before the `atomic_dec_return(&ep->re_receiving)` check in `rpcrdma_post_recvs()`, and the existing `out:` label remains below it. No other statements were changed.

Author: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>

    xprtrdma: Streamline rpcrdma_post_recvs
    
    rb_lock is contended between rpcrdma_buffer_create,
    rpcrdma_buffer_put, and rpcrdma_post_recvs.
    
    Commit e340c2d6ef2a ("xprtrdma: Reduce the doorbell rate (Receive)")
    causes rpcrdma_post_recvs to take the rb_lock repeatedly when it
    determines more Receives are needed. Streamline this code path
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body includes the relevant receive-posting logic and the fix pattern. In the buggy version, a receive WQE could be taken from the free list / created and then fail DMA mapping, but the corresponding cleanup path could miss balancing the receive-drain accounting. In this commit, the code is restructured so that the `count` increment only happens after successful mapping: `if (!rpcrdma_regbuf_dma_map(...)) goto release_wrs;` followed by `++count;`. It also ensures failed WQEs are released via `release_wrs:` and the final accounting is centralized at `ep->rep_receive_count += count;`. Since the vulnerable early-return/unbalanced path is not present here, this function already contains the fix.
